where: Worked example 1, steps 1–2; quiz Q3 and Q6; Section 2 formula note
problem: The powers of ten have lost their superscripts, so the expressions read as ordinary arithmetic and give wrong numbers. Step 1 shows 'Pin = 1020/10 mW = 100 mW', which a student will read as 1020 ÷ 10 = 102 mW. Step 2 shows '100 × 10−6/10 mW', Q3 shows '104/10 mW', Q6 shows '10−16/10 mW', and the note after the Wilkinson formula says '|S|2 is a power ratio' instead of |S|². Only subscripts are marked up; no exponent is.
fix: Use <sup> for every exponent: P<sub>in</sub> = 10<sup>20/10</sup> mW = 100 mW; P<sub>after</sub> = 100 × 10<sup>−6/10</sup> mW = 25.12 mW; Q3: P = 10<sup>4/10</sup> mW = 2.51 mW; Q6: P = 10<sup>−16/10</sup> mW = 0.0251 mW; and write '|S|<sup>2</sup> is a power ratio'.

problem: The answer names the unitary condition but then gives a restatement ('matching all ports would leave no place for reflected or dissipated power') instead of the actual argument, so it does not really show why the condition fails.
fix: For a lossless reciprocal three-port, S<sup>†</sup>S = I together with S11 = S22 = S33 = 0 forces |S12||S13| = 0, |S12||S23| = 0 and |S13||S23| = 0. At least two of the three couplings must then be zero, which no real three-port tee satisfies, so all three ports cannot be matched at once.

problem: 'Power is a wave quantity' is loose and can mislead: power is not a wave quantity, and the point being made is simply that splits and losses are power ratios, so they are counted in dB of power.
fix: Splits and losses are ratios of power, so count them in decibels of power, not in decibels of voltage.
